events.region: Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound; Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out 20 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
For the following areas...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL out
20 NM...
Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound...

At 721 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm producing waterspouts was
located near West Santa Rosa Sound, or 15 nm east of Pensacola Pass,
moving west at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Beach webcams confirmed waterspout south of Gulf Breeze.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
West Santa Rosa Sound and Pensacola Beach.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: East Glacier Park Region; Northern High Plains; Eastern Glacier, Western Toole, and Central Pondera; Eastern Toole and Liberty; Southern Rocky Mountain Front; Southern High Plains; Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of north central Montana, including the following
areas, East Glacier Park Region, Eastern Glacier, Western Toole,
and Central Pondera, Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton, Eastern
Toole and Liberty, Northern High Plains, Southern High Plains and
Southern Rocky Mountain Front.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in minor flooding of creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage areas. Rural gravel and dirt roads can become muddy and
may become difficult to travel. Rock/debris slides are possible in
the mountains.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorms today will be capable of producing 0.50 to 1 inch
per hour rain rates. Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall will
be possible Monday through Tuesday morning. Widespread 0.75 to
1.5 inches of rain have already fallen along the Rocky Mountain
Front over the past 24 hours. Additional widespread rain
accumulations of 1 to 3 inches are possible along the Rocky
Mountain Front and Sweet Grass Hills with isolated 4 inches
possible along and north of US Highway 2 this afternoon through
Tuesday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
